models.inverse_notes: A=P*i/(1-(1+i)^-n) needs i>0 and n>=1; substitution P=77217.35, i=0.05, n=10 gives A=10000.00 within rounding. At n=1, A=P*(1+i) exactly (checked: 9523.81 x 1.05 = 10000.00 within rounding). A=0 admits P=0; P=0 with i>0, n>=1 forces A=0. Solving for i needs iteration and for n a logarithm, both unsupported by the scalar grammar, so those directions are untested. The i-to-0 limit branch P=A*n is a different expression, never a guard relaxation.
limitations: Beginning-of-period (annuity-due) streams need the distinct due factor with the extra (1+i) multiple and are not covered.
Excludes growing, variable, life-contingent, and indexed withdrawal streams; mortality and longevity risk are out of scope.

assumptions: Source assumption (Table III scope): most account owners -- the spouse is not the sole beneficiary, or is not more than 10 years younger; Table II (much-younger sole-beneficiary spouse) and Table I (beneficiaries) are excluded.
Source assumption: the balance is the account value at the close of business on December 31 of the preceding year (prior-year-end convention).
Application profile: the record computes the division only; RMD ages, deadlines, aggregation, and penalties are tax-law rules outside this arithmetic.

gaps: Needs new quantity meanings: prior_year_balance, rmd_distribution_period, required_minimum_distribution; no current-runtime projection attempted.

models.inverse_notes: Bal=R*L given L>0 (checked: 18867.92 x 26.5 = 499999.88, within rounding of 500000); L=Bal/R needs R>0 (checked: 500000/18867.92 = 26.50 within rounding). At R=0, Bal=0 with L undetermined. No root branches.
limitations: Excludes 403(b) pre-1987-balance rules, still-working delays, Roth treatment, and beneficiary stretch rules.
The distribution-period input must come from the current IRS table; stale factors give stale minimums.

references.method: Curator-worked division on the published Table III factor for age 73: $500,000 / 26.5 = $18,867.92. The source verifies the 26.5 factor and the rule (its own worked pairs: $38,400 / 26.5 = $1,450 and $34,800 / 26.5 = $1,313); the $500,000 balance is curator arithmetic.
references.provenance: Curator-worked arithmetic on the published Table III factor (s-irs-590b, corroborated by s-irs-rmd-faq).

references.method: Curator-worked division on the published Table III factor for age 75: $600,000 / 24.6 = $24,390.24. The source verifies the 24.6 factor and the rule (its own worked pair: $100,000 / 24.6 = $4,065); the $600,000 balance is curator arithmetic.
references.provenance: Curator-worked arithmetic on the published Table III factor (s-irs-590b, corroborated by s-irs-rmd-faq).

references.method: Boundary: a zero prior-year balance gives R = 0 exactly at the age-73 factor.
references.provenance: Curator boundary check; not observed account data.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero distribution period makes the division undefined; no IRS table publishes a zero factor.
Without the distribution period no minimum can be formed.

relationship.locator: Required Minimum Distributions: figure-RMD-by-dividing rule; Table III applicable-denominator examples (age 75 -> 24.6; Justin age 73 -> 26.5); Which Table (Table III scope); Appendix B Uniform Lifetime Table.
relationship.original_equation: R = Bal / L (required minimum distribution = prior-year-end balance / Table III distribution period)
relationship.translation_notes: Division formalization of the IRS rule: the prior-year-end balance over the published life-expectancy factor. Dimensional check: USD divided by a dimensionless period stays USD. Guard L>0 preserves the pre-simplification division exclusion; Bal>=0 admits the zero-balance boundary. The record computes the division for a stated factor; RMD ages, deadlines, and aggregation are tax-law rules outside this arithmetic.

sources.evidence: RMD = IRA balance at Dec 31 of the prior year / the Table III applicable denominator for the owner's birthday age; worked: 75-year-old, $100,000 / 24.6 = $4,065; Justin (73), $38,400 / 26.5 = $1,450 and $34,800 / 26.5 = $1,313; Table III used unless the spouse is the sole beneficiary and more than 10 years younger; Appendix B rows verified: 73->26.5, 75->24.6, 80->20.2.

assumptions: The multiple is a dimensionless years-of-expenses snapshot: savings divided by one year of spending, with no return, no inflation, no taxes, and no spending growth.
Application profile: static coverage arithmetic (the rule-of-25 form of the withdrawal-rate records); longevity or safety claims need the cited withdrawal studies, not this division.

gaps: Needs new quantity meanings: retirement_savings, annual_expenses, expense_coverage_multiple; no current-runtime projection attempted.

models.inverse_notes: S=T*W given W>0 (checked: 25 x 40000 = 1000000); W=S/T needs T>0 (checked: 1000000/25 = 40000). At T=0, S=0 with W undetermined (any positive spending is compatible). No root branches.
limitations: Not a retirement plan: ignores returns, inflation, taxes, spending change, and lifespan.
The zero-spending case is excluded by W > 0 (infinite coverage is undefined here).

references.method: Labeled cross-record closure with the record-2 Bengen check: $1,000,000 / $40,000 = 25 (the rule-of-25 multiple). Input pair shared with bengen-rule-25; recomputation, never equivalence.
references.provenance: Curator cross-record arithmetic closing the record-2 Bengen pair (s-wiki-4pct).

references.method: Labeled cross-record closure with the record-2 Trinity check: $625,000 / $25,000 = 25. Input pair shared with trinity-pair; recomputation, never equivalence.
references.provenance: Curator cross-record arithmetic closing the record-2 Trinity pair (s-wiki-trinity).

references.method: Boundary: zero savings against positive annual expenses gives T = 0 exactly.
references.provenance: Curator boundary check; not observed household data.

relationship.original_equation: T = S / W (years-of-expenses multiple = retirement savings / annual expenses; 25x is the rule-of-25 form)
relationship.translation_notes: Division formalization of the coverage multiple: savings over one year of spending. Dimensional check: USD divided by USD is dimensionless (years of expenses). Guard W>0 preserves the pre-simplification division exclusion; S>=0 admits the zero-savings boundary. Not an inverse of any covered record: no covered record divides two money stocks.

sources.evidence: Bengen's 4% first-year rule implies the rule-of-25 multiple: $1,000,000 of savings covers $40,000 of annual spending 25 times over; the $40,000/$1,000,000 pair is the record-2 Bengen check recomputed here as a labeled cross-record closure.
